anti_patterns: explicit counter-based recursion with if-then-else (I >= N -> ...) instead of clause-head pattern matching or numlist/foldl
if-then-else chains in step/4 instead of separate clauses
cut-then-fallback clauses (final catch-all clause with 0) used for control flow
assoc used with sequential integer keys where a list or dict would suffice, forcing repeated get/put pairs
red cuts after type-checking guards in eertree_count_occurrences
findall+member+max_list instead of aggregate_all(max) or direct max_member
linear nth0 scan to find the node on each occurrence query
justification: The code threads state explicitly through st/3 terms and uses assoc for node storage, which is a reasonable purely functional approach with no assert/retract. However, the build loop is written as an imperative-style counter loop with if-then-else instead of foldl/numlist or head-pattern recursion, and step/4 is one big nested if-then-else with repeated get_assoc/put_assoc. Query predicates rely on cut plus catch-all clauses and findall/max_list where aggregate_all or max_member would be more idiomatic; the comment on find_suffix helps, but the long step predicate hurts readability and design.
